title: Solvable conditions for linear congruence ax ≡ b
summary: Let d=gcd(a,m). An equation has a solution modulo m if and only if d divides b; there are exactly d distinct remainders.
applies: Integer modulo arithmetic; modulus greater than 1
detail: 6x ≡ 4 (mod 8) is approximately 3x ≡ 2 (mod 4), so x is 2 or 6 mod 8.
boundary: When removing the common factors, the module must be removed at the same time. Keeping the original module will miss the solution.
relevance: When restoring affine integer transformations, avoid mistaking multi-solution equations for permutations that can be directly inverted.
